title: Incremental Upgrade & No‑Egress Validation Protocol for Sealed VPCs
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Define unambiguous requirements and acceptance criteria for performing incremental control-plane and node-image upgrades in sealed/no‑egress (air‑gapped) Private/VPC deployments. Deliver a testable protocol that operators can run without requiring outbound egress, plus an integration checklist and rollback criteria for staged rollouts.
background: Customers operating in regulated environments require upgrades that do not rely on external connectivity. Existing upgrade docs focus on fully-connected operator workflows; we must provide a deterministic, auditable protocol that covers image staging, artifact provenance, canary selection, telemetry fallbacks, and safe rollback in sealed networks.
goals: Produce a prescriptive upgrade protocol that works in 'sealed VPC' mode (no outbound egress) and minimizes manual operator steps
Define a signed-artifact staging and verification flow that supports checksum replay and reproducible verification without contacting external mirrors
Specify automated canary selection rules and progressive rollout windows that are compatible with deterministic network partitions
Provide a test harness and acceptance tests that SRE/Customers can run inside isolated environments
non_goals: Building new external mirror infrastructure (we rely on customer mirrors or physical media for artifact transport)
Changing base image signing technology (we will define usage requirements for current signing approach)
Implementing full operator UI for all edge cases in this phase
acceptance_criteria: Signed bundle verification: Operator can validate image bundle signature and deterministic SHA-256 manifest using only local files and a pre-provisioned public key; verification logs are human- and machine-readable
Artifact parity check: Mirror seed and target node checksums match for all staged artifacts (operator-run parity report generated and stored in upgrade bundle)
Canary selection: The system exposes a stable canary selector API that picks a minimal subset (3 nodes or 10% of nodes, whichever is smaller) deterministically from operator-supplied node labels
Traffic quiesce: Upgrade can be executed with passive-traffic-quiesce windows (per-node) where in-flight inference KV caches are drained to disk and resumed after upgrade without data loss
No-egress telemetry mode: Upgrades succeed with telemetry endpoints disabled; local aggregated telemetry is captured and persisted to a customer-provided sink for later retrieval

Rollback confidence: After a simulated failure injected during canary stage, automated rollback returns nodes to previous image and the system validates service liveness and KV cache integrity within the defined rollback SLA
Operatorless bootstrap path: For fresh sealed clusters, documented bootstrap using signed offline bundles and a documented mirror mount procedure is fully reproducible from the checklist
Upgrade dry-run: A full dry-run mode exists that performs checks (manifest, parity, dependency graph, node compatibility) and emits a pass/fail report without making changes
SLA alignment: For Dedicated customers with upgrade SLA add-on, the protocol documents maximum allowed canary-induced latency increase and per-node downtime limits
rollout_plan: Stage 0 — Preflight: Operator runs 'dry-run' locally; manifest signature and parity checks must pass
Stage 1 — Seed mirror: Operator places signed bundle on internal mirror or physical media and runs mirror-consistency tool
Stage 2 — Deterministic canary: Select deterministic canary subset, apply upgrade to canaries during low-traffic window, run health probes for 30 minutes
Stage 3 — Gradual expansion: If canary passes, expand to 25% node groups with 60-minute hold windows and KV-cache warmup verification
Stage 4 — Full roll: Expand to remaining nodes in staged batches with operator approval gates and automated rollback checkpoints
Stage 5 — Post-upgrade audit: Generate upgrade report bundle (signable) including checksums, probe results, and operator notes; store in customer archive
test_plan: Local dry-run acceptance tests: manifest verification, dependency graph resolution, and node compatibility checks
Canary failure injection: automated fault injection that simulates kernel panic, image corruption, and partial network partition during canary; verify rollback path
Edge offline scenarios: test artifacts delivered by USB/mounted ISO and validated by signature check without any outbound network
Telemetry fallback test: disable external telemetry, ensure local aggregator persists logs and metrics and they can be exported post-upgrade
KV cache continuity test: populate KV cache pre-upgrade, perform upgrade, then validate resumed cache hits and correctness
risks: Operator error during mirror staging could lead to inconsistent artifacts across nodes
Undetected edge-case in signature verification may block upgrades in sealed environments
Telemetry blackout makes remote troubleshooting slower for Redwood support
Rollback may not fully restore ephemeral cache state for certain workloads — must be documented as acceptable delta or mitigated
success_metrics: 0 failed sealed-cluster upgrades in first two customer pilots
Mean time to detect canary failure < 20 minutes during staged rollouts
Operator dry-run pass rate >= 95% before starting canary upgrades
Artifact parity mismatch rate < 0.1% across staged mirrors
